extracted.intended_audience: Petitioners seeking nonregulated status under 7 CFR part 340 and interested or affected members of the public (researchers, growers, NGOs, industry) submitting comments to APHIS docket APHIS-2025-0021.
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and notice about a petition to APHIS for a determination of nonregulated status for a genetically engineered plant (MON 95275 maize) and instructions for public review and comment on the petition and draft Plant Pest Risk Assessment (PPRA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition content and form (7 CFR 340.6(b)–(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraphs (b) and (c) of § 340.6 describe the form that a petition for a determination of nonregulated status must take and the information that must be included in the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners must follow the specific information and format requirements in § 340.6(b) and (c). The petition should provide the information and data that support the claim that the article is unlikely to pose a plant pest risk (the petition states that the information provided indicates MON 95275 corn is unlikely to pose a plant pest risk). See APHIS petition number (e.g., 25-083-01p) when locating or referencing the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment period length and deadline (§ 340.6(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph (d) of § 340.6 provides that APHIS will publish a notice providing 60 days for public comment on petitions for a determination of nonregulated status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For this notice, APHIS will consider all comments received on or before September 8, 2025. Comments received after the deadline may not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for submitting comments (regulations.gov or mail)
rubrics_metrics.description: You may submit comments by the Federal eRulemaking Portal (www.regulations.gov) or by postal mail/commercial delivery to the specified APHIS address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Online: go to regulations.gov, enter APHIS-2025-0021 in the Search field, select the Documents tab, then select the Comment button for the document. Mail: send to Docket No. APHIS-2025-0021, Regulatory Analysis and Development, PPD, APHIS, 5601 Sunnyside Avenue, Beltsville, MD 20705. Include the docket number on submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment content focus: biological or ecological issues and supporting data
rubrics_metrics.description: APHIS states: 'We are particularly interested in receiving comments regarding biological or ecological issues, and we encourage the submission of scientific data, studies, or research to support your comments.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing comments, emphasize biological/ecological impacts and provide scientific evidence (data, peer-reviewed studies, research) to support assertions. Comments that are factual and supported by data are more useful for APHIS's evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document availability and locations for review
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition, draft plant pest risk assessment, and any comments received on this docket may be viewed at regulations.gov, in APHIS's reading room, and on APHIS's website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: APPLY search term 'APHIS petition 25-083-01p' on APHIS petition pages; reading room located at USDA South Building (1620), hours 8 a.m.–4:30 p.m. Call (202) 799-7039 before visiting. The Federal Register PDF is the official electronic format; use the link in the document sidebar to access it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant Pest Risk Assessment evaluation criterion (compare to unmodified variety)
rubrics_metrics.description: APHIS prepared a draft PPRA that compared the pest risk posed by MON 95275 corn with that of the unmodified variety from which it was derived; the draft PPRA concluded that MON 95275 corn is unlikely to pose an increased plant pest risk compared to the unmodified corn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PPRA methodology centers on comparative risk assessment: assess whether the genetically engineered organism increases plant pest risk relative to the conventional comparator. Evidence and analyses should address pathways to increased pest risk, ecological interactions, and likelihood/magnitude of harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-making standard: review of comments and other relevant information to approve or deny petition
rubrics_metrics.description: After the comment period closes, APHIS will review and evaluate any information received during the comment period and any other relevant information and will respond to the petitioner either approving or denying the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions will be considered alongside existing data; APHIS will base its regulatory determination on the totality of available information. APHIS will post its regulatory determination on its website and publish a notice of availability in the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory authority and scope (Plant Protection Act; 7 CFR part 340)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Plant Protection Act (7 U.S.C. 7701 et seq.), the regulations in 7 CFR part 340 regulate the introduction of organisms altered or produced through genetic engineering that are plant pests or which there is reason to believe are plant pests; such organisms and products are considered 'regulated articles.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions and assessments are evaluated within the statutory/regulatory framework of the Plant Protection Act and 7 CFR part 340. Petitioners and commenters should frame arguments and evidence in terms of plant pest risk and the regulatory criteria within these authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment confidentiality and processing (redaction/withholding/approval)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies review all submissions and may choose to redact, or withhold, certain submissions (or portions thereof). Submitted comments may not be available to be read until the agency has approved them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume immediate public posting of your comment; sensitive or confidential information may be redacted or withheld by the agency. If submitting proprietary or confidential business information, follow agency guidance for confidential submissions.
